chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who began with Al-Marwa before Al-Safa. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat. Do you not see that had he begun with his left before his right during the ablution, he would intend to repeat the ablution?'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills between which pilgrims walk during Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa, one of the two hills between which pilgrims walk during Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْوُاءُوءِ: Ablution, the ritual washing performed before prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim starts Sa'i with Marwa before Safa?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that beginning Sa'i with Marwa instead of Safa invalidates the ritual, requiring repetition. He employs a practical analogy from *wudu* (ablution), where starting with the left hand before the right is deemed a deviation from the prescribed order, thereby reinforcing the importance of adhering to the Sunnah's sequence in Hajj rituals. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the strict adherence to the Prophet's established order in acts of worship.
